newsitem.title: USA: Stocks hurt by Greenspan; technology shares rally.
newsitem.headline: Stocks hurt by Greenspan; technology shares rally.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Thursday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan signalled the central bank may raise interest rates next week but a rebound in technology shares helped cushion the market's fall.

A 1:15 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 25.68 points at 6,852 after earlier falling more than 50 points on the Greenspan's comments suggesting the central bank may raise short-term interest rates as soon as next week in a bid to ward off inflation.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 14-8 on active trading of 295 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The bond market also steadied, with the 30-year Treasury up nearly a quarter point, sending its yield to 6.97 percent from 6.99 percent on Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
In prepared testimony to the Joint Economic Committee of Congress, Greenspan said that the economy retains "a great deal of vigor" and that the job market was strong.
Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co., said Greenspan's comments in recent months have helped push long-term rates higher in the bond market.
"He is using his jawboning capacity to get markets to move. Whether he has to put an exclamation mark on it by raising (short-term) rates is debatable," Barthel said.
Fed policy-makers meet on Tuesday to consider whether to raise short-term rates, which would be the first increase in nearly two years.
Tony O'Bryan, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons, said the sell-off in stocks ahead of the Fed meeting was good for the market.

"You get selling out of the way so that an increase is discounted," O'Bryan said. "And a quarter of a point is not much of an increase. It will show that the Federal Reserve is being watchful and that Greenspan is doing his job."
A rebound in technology stocks buoyed the Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with high-tech shares. The index rose 12.05 points to 1,261.34.
"The Nasdaq is seeing a recovery or a bounceback in the technology sector. We're seeing some bottom-fishing," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
Compaq Computer Corp. rose 3-3/8 to 75-3/8 while Hewlett-Packard gained two points to 57-3/8. International Business Machines rose 1-5/8 t0 139-5/8 and Advanced Micro Devices added 1-3/8 to 41.

Analysts said the tech stocks were due for a rally after two weeks of heavy selling. Bearish comments in Wednesday's Wall Street Journal by Morgan Stanley's strategist Barton Biggs were deemed excessive by some observers.

Among the big movers, Philip Morris lost 5-3/4 at 116-1/4 on news that state attorneys general are close to a litigation settlement with Liggett, the tobacco unit of Brooke Group Ltd. Brooke Group rose 1/2 at 4-3/4.
Designer Holdings Ltd. fell 2-7/8, or 27 percent, to 7-3/4 after the sportswear designer slashed its 1997 sales outlook.
